summary:
The Utah State Parks Adjustment Act (Public Law 118-181) directs the Secretary of the Interior and the Secretary of Agriculture to convey certain Federal land to the State of Utah for inclusion in specified state parks. The operative mechanism requires conveyances by quitclaim deed, subject to valid existing rights and without consideration, within 180 days of enactment.

Section 2(a) requires the Secretary of the Interior to convey all right, title, and interest of the United States in Bureau of Land Management (BLM) land to the State for inclusion in Antelope Island State Park, as depicted on the map titled "Antelope Island State Park Proposal: Utah State Park Additions" dated February 28, 2023. Section 2(b) similarly requires the Secretary of the Interior to convey BLM land for inclusion in Wasatch Mountain State Park, as depicted on the map titled "Wasatch Mountain State Park Proposal Utah State Park Additions" dated May 3, 2024. For both conveyances, the State must pay all associated costs, including surveys and administrative costs.

Section 2(c) requires the Secretary of Agriculture to convey National Forest System land and improvements to the State for inclusion in Fremont Indian State Park, as depicted on the map titled "S. 2136--Utah State Parks Adjustment Act" dated September 12, 2023. As conditions precedent to this conveyance, the Secretary must reserve easements for all National Forest System roads and trails originating, terminating, or traversing the conveyed land. The Secretary shall convey only specific water rights (63-44, 63-1607, and 63-2817) providing water to the Castle Rock Campground and Belknap Historic Guard Station interpretive site. If the Secretary determines a survey is necessary, the State must pay the reasonable survey costs. The Secretary may enter into an agreement with the State regarding additional terms, including management of the Belknap site, road and trail maintenance, livestock grazing, and Forest Service access to retained water rights.

Section 2(d) authorizes the applicable Secretary to make minor modifications to the referenced maps to reflect surveys. Section 2(e) mandates that the State use the conveyed land for public purposes, including parks, campgrounds, recreation, and permitted livestock grazing. It establishes a reversionary interest providing that if a conveyed parcel ceases to be used for such public purposes, it shall revert to the United States at the discretion of the applicable Secretary. The Act authorizes conveyances but does not contain specific appropriations.
